gloss: appetizer (served at a bar or izakaya); pushing out

definitions.gloss: appetizer; small dish served automatically at an izakaya or bar
definitions.explanation: A small dish of food that is served automatically when you sit down at an izakaya or bar, similar to a cover charge. The customer does not order it.
The act of pushing or thrusting something outward. Also used in sumo wrestling for a technique of pushing the opponent out of the ring.

examples.japanese: {突|つ}き{出|だ}しは{枝豆|えだまめ}だった。
この{店|みせ}の{突|つ}き{出|だ}しはいつも{美味|おい}しい。
examples.english: The appetizer at this restaurant is always delicious.

examples.japanese: {居酒屋|いざかや}に{入|はい}ると、{注文|ちゅうもん}しなくても{突|つ}き{出|だ}しが{出|で}てくる。
examples.english: When you enter an izakaya, an appetizer is served even without ordering.

examples.japanese: {力士|りきし}が{相手|あいて}を{突|つ}き{出|だ}しで{破|やぶ}った。
examples.english: The sumo wrestler defeated his opponent with a thrust-out.

examples.japanese: {棚|たな}の{突|つ}き{出|だ}しに{頭|あたま}をぶつけた。
examples.english: I bumped my head on the shelf's protrusion.

examples.japanese: {横綱|よこづな}は{突|つ}き{出|だ}しで{一気|いっき}に{勝負|しょうぶ}を{決|き}めた。
examples.english: The yokozuna settled the match at once with a thrust-out.

notes:
In sense 1, {突|つ}き{出|だ}し refers to the small appetizer dish automatically served at Japanese izakaya and bars. It functions as a cover charge — the cost is added to the bill regardless of whether the customer wants it. This practice surprises some visitors to Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {突|つ}き{出|だ}しが{出|で}る: an appetizer is served
- {突|つ}き{出|だ}し{代|だい}: appetizer charge
- {突|つ}き{出|だ}しで{勝|か}つ: to win by thrust-out (sumo)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- お{通|とお}し: appetizer — same meaning as sense 1, more common in eastern Japan; {突|つ}き{出|だ}し is more common in western Japan
- {前菜|ぜんさい}: appetizer — a general term for starters at a restaurant, usually ordered by the customer

CULTURAL NOTE:
The {突|つ}き{出|だ}し system is unique to Japanese dining culture. It typically costs 300-500 yen and serves as both a snack and a seat charge. Some tourists find it confusing since it appears on the bill without being ordered.
